objective: Review the defined build-only validation boundary for the accepted Verilator overlay patch and decide whether the next gate may run that build without claiming parser behavior, execution, timing, or automatic allocation.

review_decision.weakest_point: The boundary is intentionally still build-only. Even if the next gate succeeds, it will prove compile/link compatibility of the patched Verilator source only, not parser behavior, sidecar handoff, runtime execution, timing, upstream acceptance, or arbitrary RTL/filelist support. The definition also treats VERILATOR_INSTALL as optional while using it in configure --prefix, so the run gate must either require it or set a checkout-local default as a mechanical command adjustment.
accepted_because: the source definition uses the accepted descriptor and patch paths
the upstream Verilator ref stays pinned to v5.048 peeled commit d0aa828c217410fffc73d92077b6f4f54830357c
the validation runs in an external clean checkout and does not vendor Verilator or write under third_party
the selected target is verilator_bin, which checks compile/link compatibility without running upstream test_regress
the command sequence applies the patch before building and keeps descriptor JSON validation and apply-check as preconditions
parser behavior, std::atoi strictness, docs/test_regress, runtime/ABI wiring, execution, timing, arbitrary filelist planning, and automatic allocation remain explicitly deferred

parser_behavior_execution: accept --sim-accel sidecar-gpu --sim-accel-states N --sim-accel-steps S through the built binary

required_next_gate.name: run_verilator_native_option_parser_overlay_patch_build_only_validation_gate
must_run: the exact external clean-checkout command sequence from the source definition gate, or record any reviewed reason for a mechanical command adjustment
autoconf and configure in the external checkout
an explicit VERILATOR_INSTALL value or a recorded checkout-local default before ./configure --prefix
must_record: exit code for the build-only validation command sequence
whether the command sequence reached the verilator_bin build target
any generated log path as generated evidence only, without local absolute paths in source-of-truth files
whether VERILATOR_INSTALL was provided or mechanically defaulted under the external checkout
whether any failure is dependency/tooling, patch compile/link, or command-boundary related
must_not_claim: Verilator upstream regression tests pass with this patch
new simulation execution or timing evidence

non_claims: not a landed upstream Verilator patch
not a runtime or ABI change
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
